quarterly_data.signal: Corporate Finance Leader Unal Arslan: H1 2026 revenue was 427 billion TL, down 12% versus the inflation-adjusted prior-year base; export revenues were 359 billion TL (84% of revenue) and domestic revenue 68 billion TL (down 21%); total volumes fell 6%, with exports down 4% and domestic down 18%. CFO Gul Ertug Geriskovan: export sales declined 4% to 293K units and production 3% to 341,000 units, with capacity utilization of 73% (70% in Turkiye, 79% in Romania).
quarterly_data.figure: H1 2026 revenue 427 billion TL (-12%); exports 293K units (-4%)

quarterly_data.signal: Unal Arslan: H1 2026 gross profit was 29.3 billion TL (-28%), operating profit 11.6 billion TL (-56%), adjusted EBITDA around 25.6 billion TL (-37%) at a 6.0% margin (Q2: 5.9%), and net income 10.3 billion TL (-40%), helped by 2.8 billion TL of deferred tax income after the 12.5% corporate income tax rate for manufacturing income; adjusted EBITDA per vehicle fell to approximately EUR 1,438 from 1,839. CFO: the pressure came mainly from the gap between inflation (18% in H1) and Euro/TL appreciation (5%) and from the entrepreneurial businesses (Ford Turkiye and Ford Trucks), while Ford Motor Company honours its cost-plus contracts.
quarterly_data.figure: adjusted EBITDA margin 6.0%; adjusted EBITDA per vehicle EUR 1,438

quarterly_data.signal: CFO Gul Ertug Geriskovan: 2026 guidance updated - Turkish industry 1.2 to 1.3 million units (from 1.3 to 1.4 million), Ford Otosan retail domestic volume 75k-85k, export volume unchanged, revenue a mid-to-high single digit decline, adjusted EBITDA margin between 6%-7% (implying H2 improvement through mix, pricing and cost actions), and capex kept at 300-400 mn Euros.
quarterly_data.figure: adjusted EBITDA margin 6%-7%; capex 300-400 mn Euros

quarterly_data.signal: Unal Arslan: net debt to trailing adjusted EBITDA rose to 1.76 times (1.49 at year-end), well below the 3.5 times threshold; net financial debt 112 billion TL; H1 capex 8.3 billion TL (1.9% of sales); free cash flow 10.9 billion TL; cash and equivalents 56 billion TL. Koc Finans debt and EBITDA will be excluded from the industrial leverage calculation.
quarterly_data.figure: net debt/EBITDA 1.76x; free cash flow 10.9 billion TL

quarterly_data.signal: CFO Gul Ertug Geriskovan: the Board approved the Ford Trucks New Cab project with a net investment of 364 million Euros (joint development with IVECO), with the next-generation cab introduced progressively from 2028 and a first right-hand-drive derivative for entry into the UK market; the acquisition of Koc Finansman was completed on 1 July and will appear in reports from the third quarter.
quarterly_data.figure: Ford Trucks New Cab net investment 364 million Euros

quarterly_data.signal: Head of IR Bahar Efeoglu Agar: the Turkish market fell 8% in H1 2026 (12% in Q2) and 25% in July; Ford Otosan's domestic sales fell 24% after the Focus discontinuation, ranking fifth with a 6.6% share while leading commercial vehicles with a 24.6% share; Ford's European CV market share normalized to 15.5% from 17.2% in 2025 as Volkswagen's versions of the 1-ton van, also produced by Ford Otosan, reached the market; Ford Otosan produces more than 15% of Ford's global vehicle registrations.
quarterly_data.figure: Turkish market -8% in H1; CV market share 24.6%
